title: Finite-extension geometric-fiber formula
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with ring of integers $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\bar y:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y P$, with projections $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$ and $a_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that $X,Y,X_{\bar y},P$ are noetherian and finite-dimensional [def-pc-dimension], that $\ell$ is invertible on all four schemes, that $a_{\bar y}$ is proper, and that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at most some $e\geq0$, as required by [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension]. Use the raw rational categories $\Dbc(T,E)=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. For the cartesian square $(f,a_{\bar y},\bar y,i_{\bar y},\mathrm{id})$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], use the rational extensions of integral direct images and completed pullbacks and the specified rational exchange of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension]. For every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$, this exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$
 L\bar y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(P,E).
$$

proof.text: Set $Y'=P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $g=\bar y$, $X'=X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y P$, $g'=i_{\bar y}$, $f'=a_{\bar y}$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{X\times_Y P}$. By the defining projection equality for the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $f i_{\bar y}=\bar y a_{\bar y}$. Thus these data form the cartesian square of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with the geometric point of [def-weil-geometric-point] as its lower horizontal map. This is simply the square defining the geometric fibre, without changing either projection.

source.place: Proof: specialize thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension to the geometric-point base change (same statement in main-20261015, order 1418)

proof.text: For each of the four schemes use [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]: $\Dbc(T,E)$ is the raw scalar localization of the integral constructible category, with the same objects and with Hom modules tensored from $A$ to $E$. The noetherian, finite-dimensional and invertibility assumptions in the statement place every scheme in the domain of this definition. In particular the given $K$ is an object of exactly the rational source category in [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension], and the target category for $Y'=P$ is $\Dbc(P,E)$.

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] to the square of step 1 and the object $K$ of step 2. Its scheme hypotheses hold by the explicit assumptions: all four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, both vertical maps $f$ and $a_{\bar y}$ are proper, and the geometric fibers of $f$ have the stated bound $e$. The coefficient field is the given finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. The theorem asserts that its specified rational exchange is an isomorphism for every such $K$. Substituting $g=\bar y$, $g'=i_{\bar y}$ and $f'=a_{\bar y}$ into that exchange gives exactly $L\bar y^*Rf_*K\to Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K$. The operations and exchange were defined in the statement to be those of that theorem for this square, so this is the specified morphism, and the isomorphism lies in its stated target $\Dbc(P,E)$.

The stalk of the derived direct image of an l-adic constructible complex along a proper scheme morphism equals the cohomology of the geometric fiber
